title: Molex Renews Sponsorship of Team 2151
author: Monty Pythons
excerpt: We are grateful to Molex for renewing its sponsorship of the Monty Pythons for the 2026–2027 season.
bodyMarkdown:
We are grateful to Molex for renewing its sponsorship of FRC Team 2151, the Monty Pythons, for the 2026–2027 season!

Their continued support helps our team prepare for competition and gives team members opportunities to develop their skills through hands-on engineering, programming, and robot design.

Thank you, Molex, for supporting our team and helping us prepare for another season!

title: October 2026 Recap: Competition, Outreach, and Preparation
author: Monty Pythons
excerpt: A look back at SHOUT!, PACK EXPO International, a visit from Chicago White Metal Casting, and our team's preparations for the 2027 FRC season.
bodyMarkdown:
October was an eventful month for the Monty Pythons as we participated in an off-season competition, showcased our robot at a major industry event, connected with local manufacturing professionals, and continued preparing for the upcoming 2027 FIRST Robotics Competition season.

## SHOUT! Robotics Competition

On October 17, our team traveled to Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to compete at the SHOUT! Robotics Competition, held at Divine Savior Holy Angels High School. The event brought together 29 FRC teams and emphasized expanding opportunities for girls and underrepresented genders in robotics.

We competed with our 2026 robot, Monty, finishing qualification matches with a 2–3 record and ranking 25th overall. Although our performance did not meet our expectations, the competition provided valuable experience and helped us identify areas for improvement.

SHOUT! reinforced the importance of reliability, preparation, and testing under competition conditions. These are lessons we hope to carry into our planning and development for the next season.

## PACK EXPO International 2026

On October 18, the Monty Pythons participated in the Future Innovators Robotics Showcase at PACK EXPO International, held at McCormick Place in Chicago.

Sponsored by Schneider Electric, the showcase brought together FRC and FTC teams to demonstrate their robots and highlight the engineering, programming, and problem-solving skills involved in competitive robotics.

Our participation gave us an opportunity to share our team's work beyond the FIRST community at an event featuring developments in manufacturing, automation, and industrial technology.

We appreciate the organizers and Schneider Electric for providing this opportunity to showcase our work and represent Proviso Mathematics and Science Academy.

## Visit from Chicago White Metal Casting

On October 20, representatives from Chicago White Metal Casting visited our team at Proviso Mathematics and Science Academy to learn more about our robotics program.

During their visit, we had the opportunity to introduce our team, demonstrate our work, and discuss the engineering and technical skills involved in designing and building competition robots.

The visit also opened discussions about potential future collaboration, including opportunities for team members to visit Chicago White Metal's manufacturing facilities and gain firsthand exposure to professional engineering and manufacturing processes.

We appreciate Chicago White Metal Casting for taking the time to visit our team and explore opportunities to support hands-on STEM education.

## Preparing for Build Season

Outside of these events, our regular meetings focused primarily on training and preparation for the upcoming build season.

Team members worked within their respective departments, participating in lessons, presentations, and discussions intended to strengthen their skills and understanding of robotics. These meetings also provided opportunities for newer members to become more familiar with their departments while returning members continued developing their knowledge.

Although much of this work took place outside of competitions and public events, it remains an important part of preparing our team for the challenges ahead.

## Looking Ahead

October gave our team opportunities to reflect on our performance, share our work with a broader audience, and develop connections within the local engineering community. As we approach the 2027 season, we will continue focusing on improving our technical skills, strengthening collaboration across departments, and preparing for kickoff in January.

We look forward to building on what we learned throughout the month and applying those lessons during the upcoming season.

title: Baxter International Joins Team 2151 as a Sponsor
author: Monty Pythons
excerpt: We are grateful to Baxter International for supporting our robotics team through a grant!
bodyMarkdown:
We are excited to recognize our new sponsor, Baxter International, for supporting FRC Team 2151, the Monty Pythons, through a monetary grant.

This support helps us purchase materials and continue developing our team. We appreciate Baxter International’s investment in our team and the opportunities it helps make possible.

Thank you, Baxter International, for supporting Team 2151 and helping us keep building!

title: Online Metals Joins Team 2151 as a Sponsor
author: Monty Pythons
excerpt: We are excited to have Online Metals as a sponsor and grateful for their credit to purchase materials!
bodyMarkdown:
We are excited to welcome Online Metals as a new sponsor of FRC Team 2151!

Online Metals has provided us with credit to purchase materials for our robotics work. This support will help us turn our ideas into designs, build and test robot mechanisms, and continue learning through hands-on problem-solving. We are grateful for Online Metals' contribution and for helping us prepare for the work ahead as the build season approaches.

Thank you, Online Metals, for supporting us and helping us keep building!

title: Team 2151 Participates in the Bridging the Gap Parade
author: Monty Pythons
excerpt: Team 2151 members represented PMSA at the 2026 Bridging the Gap Parade, handing out candy, spreading positivity, and connecting with the local community.
bodyMarkdown:
On September 12, around 15 members of our team represented Proviso Mathematics and Science Academy at the 2026 Bridging the Gap Parade & Community Resource Fair.

The annual event brings together communities across Proviso Township to celebrate unity, culture, and community involvement. This year's parade traveled from Bellwood to Proviso East High School in Maywood before continuing with a community resource fair.

Throughout the parade, our team members walked the route, handed out candy, and helped spread positivity to those watching along the way. It was great to see how excited people were to interact with the team and support everyone participating in the event!

Thank you to all of the team members who came out to represent Team 2151 and PMSA. Events like Bridging the Gap give us an opportunity to support the communities around us and represent our team outside of competitions.
